target_customer: Video publishers, broadcasters and enterprises streaming live or on demand video, later enterprise IT teams distributing internal video
problem: Delivering video to many viewers is expensive for publishers; Peer5 uses WebRTC peer to peer sharing in the browser to offload bandwidth from servers.
business_model: Usage and subscription priced P2P CDN and enterprise CDN
product_category: Peer to peer video delivery network, eCDN

founders.name: Hadar Weiss
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Co-Founder and CEO; Globes calls him cofounder and CEO.

founders.name: Shachar Zohar
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Co-Founder and CTO; no bio on the page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a scalable browser peer mesh over WebRTC that keeps playback quality and works across networks was hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Peer mesh algorithms and customer integrations were difficult to copy, but Streamroot and Viblast sold the same idea.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large CDNs did not copy it; Microsoft bought Peer5 in August 2021 to improve Teams live events.

market_need_then: Video traffic was growing and bandwidth costs were high; Globes named Dailymotion and Artear as customers at the 2017 raise.

identity.voice_and_tone: Technical product claims such as 20x server capacity and 70 percent bandwidth offload on the YC page

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself; known in streaming industry coverage as a P2P CDN and via the Microsoft deal.

pivots.to: File downloading, then back to video
pivots.why: Per a Bloggeek analysis; dates and reasons not stated

outcome_analysis: Peer5 sold a WebRTC peer to peer video CDN, raised a 2.5 million dollar seed after YC in 2017 and about 3.5 million dollars in total according to VentureBeat, and found a niche as an enterprise eCDN. Microsoft acquired it in August 2021 for undisclosed terms to improve large Teams live events, a strategic acquisition driven by remote work video demand.
notes: peer5.com could not be fetched from this session (host not resolvable), so no site check. VentureBeat says 3.5 million dollars total VC from FG Angels and others; Globes says 2.5 million dollar seed in August 2017; TechCrunch and aggregators give dates from March to July 2017 for the same raise, so the earlier items are not recorded as separate rounds. Third cofounder Guy Paskar appears only in one aggregator and is not listed. Competitor traction and funding as of 2017 not found; Bloggeek source is undated in the snippet.
